quickStart.item_11: For an immediate police emergency, call 999. For an ambulance or fire emergency, call 995.
quickStart.item_22: For urgent but non-emergency medical needs, contact a healthcare provider or use the official MOH and HealthHub service directories.
quickStart.item_55: Review emergency contacts, health information, legal document locations, insurance, bank accounts, CPF, SRS, and essential liabilities.
quickStart.item_31: If someone has died, identify the executor or authorised representative and contact CPF Board, banks, insurers, employers, IRAS, and service providers using their official processes.
quickStart.item_02: CPF nominations and wills are not interchangeable. Confirm CPF nomination status with CPF Board and obtain legal advice for estate questions.
quickStart.item_45: Keep the export encrypted. Never store passwords, Singpass credentials, authentication codes, or recovery keys in it.

legalNotes.item_113: Singapore public healthcare subsidies and schemes have eligibility and programme conditions; MediSave is a savings scheme for approved healthcare expenses, not a universal insurance policy.
legalNotes.item_55: NRIC/FIN is sensitive personal data. Singapore government guidance says an IC is compulsory for citizens and permanent residents from age 15; recording the number in this organizer is optional.
legalNotes.item_11: CPF savings and CPF nominations have specific CPF Board rules and are not interchangeable with a will. Verify current nomination status and distribution procedures directly with CPF Board.
legalNotes.item_112: Singapore LPAs are registered arrangements for property/affairs and/or personal welfare decisions if mental capacity is lost. An LPA does not replace a will or determine post-death estate distribution.
legalNotes.item_40: IRAS states estate duty was removed for deaths on or after 15 February 2008; confirm any historical or current tax/reporting issue with IRAS or a qualified adviser.
legalNotes.item_22: Emergency: Singapore Civil Defence Force: https://www.scdf.gov.sg/

recoveryRoadmap.description: A general checklist after a death in Singapore. Confirm representative authority and current CPF, court, tax, and provider requirements before acting.

meta.title: Family Recovery Roadmap - Singapore
meta.reviewedBy: Government sources reviewed; case-specific legal and tax advice may be needed

intro.condolence: We are sorry for your loss. This checklist is intended to make the first practical steps clearer.
intro.howToUse: Follow official registration guidance, identify the executor or authorised representative, contact each provider, and keep a record of each action.

startHere.0: Follow the official death registration and funeral guidance.
startHere.1: Locate the will and identify the executor; check whether probate or letters of administration are required.
startHere.2: Contact CPF Board, IRAS, banks, insurers, employers, SRS operators, and service providers using their current procedures.
startHere.3: List assets, debts, regular payments, and claims; confirm authority before changing payments or distributing property.
startHere.4: Keep a log of contacts, forms, and documents supplied. Never use the deceased person's Singpass or online account credentials.

legalFramework.0: Singapore Courts probate and letters of administration processes.
legalFramework.1: CPF Board account, nomination, and death-benefit rules.
legalFramework.2: IRAS income tax and any estate or historical tax matters.
legalFramework.3: MSF Office of the Public Guardian LPA registration and decision-support requirements.
legalFramework.4: Insurance, SRS, property, and financial-institution contract rules.
